title: A humbled convert is called to preside and preach in Freedom
setting: Warren A. Cowdery, an older brother of Oliver Cowdery, lived in Freedom, New York. He had corresponded with Oliver in Kirtland and was not yet a member in spring 1834. Joseph Smith dictated this revelation for him at Kirtland on 25 November 1834. Freedom served as a gathering point for several branches in western New York.
summary: The revelation calls Warren A. Cowdery to be ordained a presiding high priest over the church in Freedom and nearby areas. He is to preach and warn people there and in adjoining counties. He is to give his whole time to the calling, and the text says “the laborer is worthy of his hire”. It warns that the Lord’s coming will overtake the world “as a thief in the night”. Those who are “children of light” need not be caught off guard. It says heaven rejoiced when Warren turned from “the crafts of men”. Despite “the vanity of his heart,” he will be lifted up if he humbles himself. If he stays a faithful witness, a crown is prepared for him.

contextNote.title: Mercy paired with a frank warning
contextNote.text: The revelation calls a new convert to lead, yet it names a fault in him. Verse 6 says heaven rejoiced when Warren “bowed to my scepter”. Verse 7 then admits “the vanity of his heart” in the same breath as mercy. The promise is conditional: he will be lifted up “inasmuch as he will humble himself”. Verse 8 adds grace “wherewith he may stand” and a crown if he stays faithful. In this passage, being lifted up depends on Warren choosing humility, not on being free of the fault.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 106–108 includes this call to Warren Cowdery as an example of the Lord calling imperfect people. How do verses 7–8 balance Warren’s weakness with the Lord’s promises?
reviewNote: Read all 8 verses. Official heading gives Kirtland, 25 November 1834, to Warren A. Cowdery, Oliver’s older brother. The JSP page loaded without its introduction body text; facts on Warren’s letters, his non-member status in spring 1834, and Freedom as a branch center came from the JSP footnotes. His baptism date was not confirmed. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes.
